# Mentions

3 routes. Base URL: `https://orbitwrite.com/api/v1`. Paths below are absolute.

| Method | Path | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/v1/mentions/handles` | Search a platform for accounts to @mention |
| GET | `/api/v1/mentions/linkedin/resolve` | Resolve a LinkedIn company slug to its organization URN |
| GET | `/api/v1/mentions/linkedin` | Search LinkedIn mention candidates |

### GET /api/v1/mentions/handles

Search a platform for accounts to @mention

Requires `account:read`. Type-ahead over the platforms whose mentions are plain handles — Bluesky and Mastodon. Insert the returned `handle` after an `@` in the post body and the platform resolves it at publish time; no id or markup is needed. Results are scoped to the channel: a Mastodon search runs against that account's own instance on its token, so two channels can legitimately return different results for the same query. Channels on other platforms are a 400 — X and Threads have no public handle search, and LinkedIn mentions are structured nodes (use `/mentions/linkedin`).

**Auth:** API key or session
**Rate limited:** yes (429 when the per-credential budget is spent)

**Query parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `accountId` | string | yes | The connected channel the mention is being written for. Names the workspace, and on Mastodon supplies the instance and token the search runs against. |
| `q` | string (max length 200) | yes | What the author has typed after the `@`. |

**Responses**

- `200` — Matching accounts, best first, capped at 8
  - object
    - `results`: array of `HandleMention`, required
      - `handle`: string, required — Inserted verbatim after `@`. A bare username on Bluesky (`alice.bsky.social`), `user@instance` for a remote Mastodon account.
      - `displayName`: string
      - `avatarUrl`: string
- `400` — Invalid request
  - `Error`
- `401` — Not signed in
  - `Error`
- `403` — Not a member of the organization
  - `Error`
- `404` — The resource does not exist
  - `Error`
- `429` — Rate limit exceeded
  - `Error`
- `502` — The platform couldn't be reached

### GET /api/v1/mentions/linkedin/resolve

Resolve a LinkedIn company slug to its organization URN

Requires `account:read`. Turns the vanity name in a company URL (`linkedin.com/company/orbitwrite` → `orbitwrite`) into the `urn:li:organization:…` a LinkedIn mention node needs, asking LinkedIn with the named channel's token. The lookup is exact-match: a slug LinkedIn has no company for returns `{ "organization": null }`, which is an answer and not an error — fall back to a numeric company URL or a URN the author supplies. A 502 means the lookup itself failed and the slug is still unknown; do not write a mention on the strength of one.

**Auth:** API key or session
**Rate limited:** yes (429 when the per-credential budget is spent)

**Query parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `accountId` | string | yes | The connected channel the mention is being written for. Names the workspace, and on Mastodon supplies the instance and token the search runs against. |
| `slug` | string (max length 100) | yes | The vanity name from the company URL, without the leading path. |

**Responses**

- `200` — The organization, or `null` when LinkedIn has no company with that vanity name
  - object
    - `organization`: object | null, required
      - `urn`: string, required
      - `url`: string, required
      - `name`: string
- `400` — Invalid request
  - `Error`
- `401` — Not signed in
  - `Error`
- `403` — Not a member of the organization
  - `Error`
- `404` — The resource does not exist
  - `Error`
- `429` — Rate limit exceeded
  - `Error`
- `502` — LinkedIn couldn't be reached

### GET /api/v1/mentions/linkedin

Search LinkedIn mention candidates

Requires `account:read`. LinkedIn mentions are structured URN nodes rather than plain handles, so build the mention from the returned `id` — there is nothing useful to type.

Two directories, distinguished by `source`. `channel` results are the workspace's own connected LinkedIn accounts, substring-matched. A `lookup` result is a company LinkedIn itself returned, and appears only when the whole query is a well-formed vanity name — their keyword company search is restricted to selected developers, so exact match on the vanity name is the only search available to us. Typing `orbit` will not find `orbitwrite`; typing `orbitwrite` will. Queries shorter than 3 characters never reach LinkedIn, and a client should debounce: the quota behind this is per *application* per day, not per caller, so every prefix you send costs everyone.

A LinkedIn that can't be reached costs you the `lookup` candidate, not the request. People cannot be searched at all — only members who have connected a channel to this workspace appear.

**Auth:** API key or session
**Rate limited:** yes (429 when the per-credential budget is spent)

**Query parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `accountId` | string | yes | The connected channel the mention is being written for. Names the workspace, and on Mastodon supplies the instance and token the search runs against. |
| `q` | string (max length 200) | yes | What the author has typed after the `@`. |

**Responses**

- `200` — Matching mention targets, capped at 8 in total — a `lookup` result displaces the last channel rather than extending the list.
  - object
    - `results`: array of `LinkedInMention`, required
      - `id`: string, required — The URN to address: `urn:li:organization:123` for a page, `urn:li:person:<sub>` for a person.
      - `name`: string, required
      - `avatarUrl`: string
      - `type`: one of `"person"` | `"organization"`, required
      - `source`: one of `"channel"` | `"lookup"`, required — `channel` is a LinkedIn account connected to this workspace, substring-matched. `lookup` is a company LinkedIn returned for the query taken as a vanity name — at most one, only when the query is a complete vanity name. Don't blend the two in a UI: a `lookup` row appears only on the last keystroke, which reads as a glitch inside a list that has been filtering all along.
      - `url`: string — Canonical linkedin.com URL, organizations only. Cross-posting a mention to a non-LinkedIn network degrades to this link; people have no equivalent public URL derivable from the URN.
- `400` — Invalid request
  - `Error`
- `401` — Not signed in
  - `Error`
- `403` — Not a member of the organization
  - `Error`
- `404` — The resource does not exist
  - `Error`
- `429` — Rate limit exceeded
  - `Error`
